data.title: Promethazine
data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Antihistamines_

**Class:** First-generation H1 antihistamine — phenothiazine

## Mechanism of action
- H1 inverse agonist with strong anticholinergic, sedative, antiemetic and anti-dopaminergic effects

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Night-time itch and sedation, allergic reactions, motion sickness, nausea, pre-medication

## Dose & formulations
- Adults 10–25 mg at night (up to 25 mg three times daily); injection 25 mg deep IM

## Adverse effects
- Marked sedation; respiratory depression in children under 2 (boxed warning — contraindicated)
- Photosensitivity and photoallergy (phenothiazine), contact dermatitis with topical use
- Extrapyramidal reactions, QT prolongation; severe tissue injury/gangrene with intra-arterial or perivascular injection

## Contraindications
- Children under 2 years; intra-arterial or SC injection

## Drug interactions
- CNS depressants, other anticholinergics, QT drugs

## Pregnancy & lactation
Has been used; avoid near term (neonatal effects).

## Viva points
- Phenothiazine antihistamine — photosensitivity; contraindicated under 2 years

_Sources: Khopkar (First generation H1 antihistamines); Wolverton 4e ch.32. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
